about: Château Smith Haut Lafitte stands on a gravel rise in Martillac, in the Graves south of Bordeaux, and its records go back to 1365. In the 18th century a Scottish merchant, George Smith, built the manor house, shipped the wine to England and gave the estate his name. Daniel Cathiard, a former Olympic skier, and his wife Florence bought it in 1990 and still live there. They have made it one of Bordeaux’s leading names, and their family also runs the Caudalie skincare brand and Les Sources de Caudalie hotel next door.

The estate farms organically on its gravel hillside and makes its own barrels in an on-site cooperage, which is rare in Bordeaux. In 2015, a dry spring and summer followed by a cool, wet August, the team picked over four weeks, from young Merlot on 14 September to Cabernet Franc in mid-October. Whole berries were fermented in small wooden vats with hand punch-downs. The wine then spent 18 months on its lees in French oak, 60% new.

The 2015 marked the château’s 650th anniversary and the Cathiards’ 25th vintage, and it wears a special commemorative label. Technical director Fabien Teitgen describes an almost black wine with fresh dark and red fruit, then spice, cedar, liquorice, violet and a hint of flint. The palate is dense and silky, finishing floral and mineral. It is one of the estate’s most highly rated reds.
facts: 63% Cabernet Sauvignon, 33% Merlot, 2% Cabernet Franc, 2% Petit Verdot
18 months on lees in French oak, 60% new, from the estate’s own cooperage
Whole berries in small wooden vats, hand punch-downs
Grand Cru Classé de Graves, AOC Pessac-Léognan
